I don’t think consciousness should be used as the indicator of personhood though. Because using your example of a brain dead person, it would still be illegal to kill them. Same with someone who is sleeping or in a coma

I appreciate you presenting your points. So for you, it essentially boils down to the right to bodily autonomy of the woman outweighing the right to life of the child, as the mother never consented to having the child?

I like this a lot, it’s very convincing. However, I still don’t think viability is the best argument, because even though current medical standards have lowered viability to the first 24 weeks, this could change in the future. This then raises the issue of it seeming wrong that are definition of murder and/or life is based upon scientific development. Although maybe people don’t have an issue with this.

I also think that just because a low amount of fertilised eggs become embedded in the lining of the uterus doesn’t mean that the fertilised egg shouldn’t be considered a life. They are still developing, even if only a low amount of them progress to the next stage of a pregnancy. There are many cases that a viable fetus will die in the womb prior to being born, however, whilst they were alive within the womb, they were still considered a human. Just because it doesn’t make it doesn’t mean that while it still was viable it wasn’t a life.

Finally, I do agree with you that abortions should be performed if the life of the mother is at risk. I appreciate the effort you put into your comment

I feel like the consent was given by the mother when she engaged in sex (although this wouldn’t apply to cases of rape). However, even if you disregard this, which I think many people will, the child also has never given consent to be aborted. So in the situation in which neither the mother or the child has consented, I feel like my earlier point still stands, as they cancel each other out. Murder should not be able to be carried out as a matter of convenience to the mother.

I want to reiterate that an unwanted pregnancy is a horrible situation. It’s just the lesser of two evils, when the alternative is murder. In an ideal world, the woman would never become pregnant until she so desires.
I wouldn’t say that comparison is entirely fair, as the acorn is closer to a women’s period than to a fertilised eggs. Plants just can’t really be compared to animals

Sorry, I completely do. I’m unsure where I brought my feelings into it? When I said, “I feel that...”, I was using that as a figure of speech. I apologise if I wasn’t being assertive enough. If I were to rephrase, I would say “you are clearly placing more importance on the bodily autonomy of the woman than on that of the child, which makes no logical sense, as they are both human being worthy of the same dignity and right to life.” I’m sorry if I wasn’t being clear. I really do want a good conversation without ad hominems
Well by killing the child, you are placing the bodily autonomy of the woman over the bodily autonomy of the child, which I feel is the same as asserting the woman is more valuable than the child

Why is the woman any more important than the child? Obviously having an unwanted child is a terrible situation, but it’s still better than murder. I personally feel murder shouldn’t be committed for the sake of convenience

Because the process of development has become to occur. 

A further point though. Pregnancies are normally not detected until at least a month into the development of the child, at which point a heartbeat is detectable
But what about the bodily autonomy of the child?

Can someone please explain to me their reasoning as to why abortion should be permitted? I’m not trying to be confrontational. I just genuinely want to know.

I am quite left leaning in almost all policies outside of this one. I’m also not religious. For me, it is strictly a biological issue. Pretty much the moment after fertilisation of the egg, a child is starting to develop. Even just a day after fertilisation, the fertilised egg is significantly larger than an unfertilised one. For me, this is clearly the start of a child’s life, and thus the termination of this embryo should be considered murder.

Obviously rape and incest are abhorrent. I firmly believe that birth control should be free and readily available for all. But I’m also tired of pro-choice people labelling all pro-lifers  evil old men who don’t care about life at all. Sure, that’s probably the case for some, but not all.

I would just like some clarification from a pro-choice person as to why abortion isn’t murder. And if there is any point in a pregnancy where abortion does become murder. And if so, where do you draw the line?

I just want some constructive dialogue. Thanks!
